headline: Approved gutter work at 115 Derby Street and an EV charger at 13 Beckford Street; found 38 Norman Street building historically significant.
summary: The commission found 38 Norman Street historically significant but not preferably preserved, and required photographs and plans before demolition. It found 2 Commercial Street and 75 North Street not historically significant. It also continued 8 Conners Road and 14 Beckford Street to October 7, 2026.
decisions: Certificate of Appropriateness issued September 14, 2026 for replacing roof shingles at 303 Lafayette Street, reviewed as a minor change.
Found the building at 2 Commercial Street not historically significant; motion carried with six in favor.
Found 75 North Street not historically significant; motion carried.
Found the building at 38 Norman Street historically significant; motion carried with six in favor.
Found the building at 38 Norman Street not preferably preserved and required photographs and dimensional plans before demolition; motion carried.
Continued the 8 Conners Road application to October 7, 2026 to allow for a site visit, 6-1.
Continued the 1A Cambridge Street application to October 7, 2026.
Withdrew the 10 Broad Street application without prejudice.
Continued the 14 Beckford Street fencing application to October 7, 2026 to conduct a site visit.
Approved the 115 Derby Street gutter and downspout work as submitted.
Approved the 13 Beckford Street EV charger installation with a box enclosure overseen by Commissioner Martinez before install; motion carried.
Approved minutes for August 19 and September 2, 2026, with a correction to the September 2 minutes.

DRAFT 
SALEM HISTORICAL COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
September 16, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Historical Commission was held on September 16, 2026 at 6:00PM via Zoom 
Virtual Meeting.  Present were Milo Martinez, Robert Peterson, Brendan Murray, Chair Kelly Tyler-
Lewis, Vice Chair Rebecca English, Mark Meche (arrived late), Margarida Raka-Goncalves (arrived late).  
Staff: Patti Kelleher. Absent: Vijay Joyce, Emily Gonzalez. 
 
 
303 Lafayette Street 
Renewal Ventures LLC applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace 3tab asphalt roof shingles 
with architectural roof shingles.   
 
This application was reviewed as a minor change under the Historical Commission policy for architectural 
roof shingles.  No abutter objection was received, and a Certificate was issued on September 14, 2026. 
 
 
2 Commercial Street 
Candide O’Rourke applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish building older than 50 
years.   
 
This application was presented in conjunction with 75 North Street as both buildings are part of the same 
redevelopment project. 
 
Attorney Scott Grover was present.  Dom Pazulo and Dan Skolski (DMS Design) were also present.  
Three parcels of land along the North River (also including 75 North Street and 3 S Mason St) were said 
to be part of a transit-oriented development project to feature 60 residential units and a small commercial 
component on the first floor.  The project is located in the North River Canal Corridor overlay zoning 
district.  Various variances and special permits were required as well as recommendations from DRB, 
order of conditions from Conservation Commission, and Chapter 91 license from MA DEP.  Two existing 
buildings onsite needed to be demolished to proceed.  Bill’s Towing Company was formerly at the site of 
2 Commercial.  Images of 75 North Street were also shown.  Mr. Skolski said the building at 75 North 
Street was constructed circa 1950 with no redeeming characteristics in architectural character, trim, or 
massing.  Said to be in fair condition, lack of appreciable maintenance over past decades.  2 Commercial 
Street building is a wood frame building used as a commercial garage many years, built circa 1940.   
 
Mr. Grover said the area along the North River canal is formerly filled tidelands subject to Chapter 91 
jurisdiction, in response to Mr. Meche’s question.  Ms. Kelleher did not find either building on a city atlas 
circa 1938.  Mr. Meche affirmed that no inventory forms exist for 2 Commercial or 75 North.  Ms. 
English and Mr. Peterson agreed with Mr. Meche’s comment that neither building has any redeeming 
historical qualities.  Chair Tyler-Lewis agreed that no special architectural features appeared on the 
buildings. 
 
No public comment.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 16, 2026 
Page 2 of 6 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to find building at 2 Commercial Street not historically significant.  Ms. 
English seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Martinez, Murray, Peterson, Meche, Tyler-Lewis were 
in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
75 North Street 
75 North Street LLC applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish building older than 50 
years.   
 
Details on this property were presented during the hearing on 2 Commercial St (see above). 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to find 75 North Street not historically significant.  Ms. English seconded 
the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Murray, Peterson, Meche were in favor and the motion 
so carried. 
 
 
38 Norman Street 
38 Norman QOZB, LLC applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish building older than 50 
years.   
 
Attorney Scott Grover was present on behalf of owner and joined by Ryan Wittig, principal of LLC.  This 
was formerly the site of Joe’s Auto Laundry, across the street from Holyoke Insurance building, near to 
the roundabout at Chestnut and Summer Streets.  In 2022, approvals were issued by the Planning Board, 
Salem Redevelopment Authority and the DRB to redevelop property into a mixed use project (first floor 
retail and commercial, upper floors residential). The Historical Commission had approved a waiver in 
2022 for demolition, but the project was delayed and the waiver expired.  Ms. Kelleher showed the 
property’s inventory form dated 1979.  Ms. Kelleher said that the building had been much altered.  Mr. 
Meche said that since the building was documented on an inventory form, the definition of historically 
significant was met.  Mr. Peterson asked if the proposed development could be considered in determining 
whether an existing structure is preferably preserved.  Ms. Kelleher spoke to the extensive reviews that 
the project had thus far undergone in the urban renewal district. 
 
Chair Tyler-Lewis said the building dated to circa 1956 and that the 2022 hearing did not feature 
commentary from HSI on the historical significance. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to find the building historically significant.  Mr. Martinez seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Murray, Peterson, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the 
motion so carried. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to find the building not preferably preserved and required that photographs 
and dimensional plans of building be provided prior to demolition.  Mr. Martinez seconded the motion.  
Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Murray, Peterson, Meche were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
8 Conners Road 
Keenan Line and Michael Hopkins applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish roof on 
building older than 50 years.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 16, 2026 
Page 3 of 6 
 
 
Ms. Line, Mr. Hopkins, and attorney Ryan Carlucci were present.  Mr. Hopkins said the owners had lived 
at a neighboring house on Conners Road for a few years and recently purchased 8 Conners Road.  The 
applicants wanted to add a second story to the house and received letters of support from neighbors for the 
project.  Mr. Hopkins showed letters from Angela and Bob Connery (at 6 Conners).  The letter supported 
the proposed renovations and noted having lived in the neighborhood for nearly 75 years.  An additional 
supporting letter was shown from Maureen Sosnowski at 9 Conners Rd.  Ms. Kelleher said that this 
property as well as 12 Conners had been inventoried and were listed in the National Register of Historic 
Places as part of the Bridge Street Neck Historic District.  Mr. Hopkins showed images of neighboring 
properties that featured two stories.  Mr. Martinez and Ms. Raka-Goncalves were hesitant to approve 
alterations of the building given its listing in the National Register. 
 
Architect Lidia Szydlowska was present.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves did not want to see the streetscape of 
similar Cape houses lose its character and that the issue was not related to size or massing of 
reconstruction.  Ms. Sydzlowska spoke to guidelines in terms of historic approvals.  Ms. Sydzlowska said 
that the neighborhood featured a mix of properties and disagreed that Capes should be classified as 
historic properties.  Ms. Sydlowska welcomed the opportunity to speak with members further during a site 
visit.  Mr. Meche requested receiving original PDF versions of the drawings, which would show more 
detail.   
 
No public comment, though Mr. Hopkins spoke again to the letters of support received from abutters. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to continue the application to October 7, 2026 to allow for a site visit.  Ms. 
English seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Murray (no), Raka-Goncalves, 
Peterson, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried 6-1. 
 
 
 
21 Warren Street–continuation 
Carrie and Lee Dichter applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to demolish a chimney.   
 
This application was previously continued to October 7, 2026. 
 
 
 
1A Cambridge Street–continuation 
Eleanor Uddo applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install solar panels.   
 
The applicant requested a continuation to the October 7 meeting. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to continue the application to October 7, 2026.  Mr. Peterson seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: English, Martinez, Murray, Peterson, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so 
carried.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 16, 2026 
Page 4 of 6 
 
10 Broad Street–continuation 
Brett McCarty applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace shutters.   
 
Ms. McCarty asked to withdraw the application. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to withdraw the application without prejudice.  Mr. Martinez seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: English, Martinez, Murray, Peterson, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so 
carried. 
 
 
 
14 Beckford Street 
Richard and Cynthia Griffin applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for fencing.   
 
The applicants were present.   
 
Mr. Griffin said the project had evolved, and the applicants were looking to replace and extend the 
existing fence (which had fallen into disrepair) across the driveway to have a larger dog-friendly space.  
The existing fence was 43’ long to be replaced in kind, to be extended in the same style by the same fence 
company, Walpole Outdoors.  Ms. Kelleher showed images of planned work, to be white with shade to 
match existing trim color.  Images of existing fencing were shown.  Composite material would be used to 
recreate the existing fence.  Mr. Griffin said that the recreated fence would be Brentwood Spindle Fence 
style from Walpole.  Mr. Griffin said that the fence would arrive finished but could be brush painted.  Ms. 
Kelleher showed an image of a sample that had been provided.  Mr. Griffin did not believe the fence was 
reinforced with metal.  Ms. Kelleher said that the sample was light in weight.  Mr. Griffin said that the 
Cambridge Historic Commission had accepted the same fence as applied for.  Chair Tyler-Lewis said 
such fences were preferred for climate durability.  Mr. Peterson lauded the sample upon inspection.  Ms. 
Kelleher said that this type of composite material had not be proposed for a fence before but had been 
reviewed and approved for deck railings (e.g. 13 Chestnut).  Mr. Murray spoke to the evolution of 
composite products becoming indistinguishable from typical wood and spoke in favor of the application.  
Mr. Meche questioned details on the planned gate that would feature as part of the install.  Ms. Griffin 
said the gate would match the style of the rest of the fence.  Mr. Martinez recommended simplifying the 
layout of the fence along the house.  Chair Tyler-Lewis and Mr. Meche proposed a site visit.  Ms. English 
wanted to see more detail on the gate.  Mr. Martinez annotated a portion of the planned gate that was 
problematic.   
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to continue the application to the next meeting date on October 7, 2026 to 
conduct a site visit.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, 
Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Peterson, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 16, 2026 
Page 5 of 6 
 
115 Derby Street 
The House of the Seven Gables Settlement Association applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for 
gutters and downspouts.   
 
Paul Wright, Director of Preservation and Maintenance, was present.  Improvements to gutters and 
downspouts were being proposed throughout the site to better address stormwater management.  CPA 
funds from City of Salem were received for this project, which was part of the Gables’ climate adaptation 
plan.  Many undersized gutters and not enough downspout outlets.  Aluminum downspouts would be 
replaced with copper on the Nathaniel Hawthorne Birthplace, 3” x 3” square would increase capacity.  
Locations for install were indicated via photograph.  Proposed location of new downspout on Hooper 
Hathaway and downspout to be repaired were also shown.  Gutter on Hooper Hathaway to be relocated up 
6” to better catch water runoff.  On Turner Ingersoll Mansion, a new 5’ wood and copper gutter would be 
installed.  Custom fabricate and fasten a 12” copper diverter to redirect water.  Move gutter up to better 
catch water shedding off upper roof.  Extend one existing downspout down to ground level with like-kind.  
Add 16” 16 oz. copper extension to copper collection boxes.  Add copper diverters to roof (inlay with 
roofing) on Visitor Center/Tea House.  Custom fabricate new 15’ no. 1 primed wood gutter with 16 oz 
copper liner and 1 new 3” smooth (on Visitor Center/Retire Beckett Archway).  Custom make one 16oz 
gutter outlet and install one new 3” round 16 oz. copper downspout (on Visitor Center/Retire Beckett 
Archway).  On rear of Tea House, custom fabricate new 31’ no. 1 primed wood gutter with 16 oz copper 
liner.  All copper seams and gutter outlets would be hot soldered.   
 
Mr. Meche referenced gutter projects undertaken by the Athenaeum in terms of slowing rain down by the 
roof, though Ms. English clarified that those alterations did not end up working.  Mr. Wright specified 
which gutters would connect to existing reservoirs, new draining systems, or rain gardens.  Members 
expressed faith in stewardship of the Gables.  Mr. Wright hoped for installation by spring 2027. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to approve the application for gutter and downspout work as submitted, 
details confirmed by Commissioner Meche with Commissioner Martinez serving as backup.  Ms. Raka-
Goncalves seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Murray, Raka-Goncalves, 
Peterson, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
 
13 Beckford Street 
Michael and Karen Williamson applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install an EV charger.   
 
Mr. Williamson presented application to install an EV charger next to the existing electric meter in the 
driveway.  Images of property was shown to specify planned install location.  Chair Tyler-Lewis and Mr. 
Meche noted that the guidelines discouraged installation on the corner of a house near the street and asked 
if the install could be located further down the driveway.  Ms. English and Ms. Raka-Goncalves felt that 
placing the charger nearer to the electrical meter might be less visually obtrusive.  Mr. Williamson said 
that the driveway (less than 10’ wide) was too narrow to fit a vehicle further into the lot.  Mr. Martinez 
suggested using a box enclosure to screen the charger and recommended that the Commission develop 
standardized version of a screening box for future applications.   
 
No public comment.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 16, 2026 
Page 6 of 6 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to approve the application to install EV charger in the vicinity of the 
cornerboard on the driveway side, design and install a box enclosure to be overseen by Commissioner 
Martinez prior to install.  Ms. English seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, 
Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Peterson, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
Other Business 
 
Minutes 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to approve minutes for August 19 and September 2, with correction to 
September 2 minutes submitted by the applicant.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  All were in favor and 
the motion so carried. 
 
Upcoming Events 
 
The HSI Preservations Awards would occur on September 22, 2026 at the Hawthorne.  The Preservation 
in a Changing Climate meeting would be held on September 23, 2026.   
 
 
Adjournment 
 
VOTE:  Mr. English motioned to adjourn.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  All were in favor and the 
motion so carried. 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 8:49 PM. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Dan Graham, Historical Commission Clerk
